text_blocks.snippet: The most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant medication for depression is Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs). SSRIs are often the first-line treatment for depression because they are generally safer and have fewer side effects compared to other types of antidepressants.

list.title: SSRIs:
list.snippet: These medications work by increasing the levels of serotonin in the brain, which is believed to play a role in regulating mood. Common SSRIs include sertraline (Zoloft), fluoxetine (Prozac), citalopram (Celexa), escitalopram (Lexapro), and paroxetine (Paxil).

list.title: Other types of antidepressants:
list.snippet: While SSRIs are the most common, other classes of antidepressants are also used, including Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors (SNRIs), atypical antidepressants, and tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs).

list.title: Individualized treatment:
list.snippet: The best medication for a person with depression can vary, and a healthcare provider will consider various factors when choosing the most appropriate treatment.

text_blocks.snippet: The most common antidepressants prescribed for depression include:
Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs): Sertraline (Zoloft), Fluoxetine (Prozac), Paroxetine (Paxil), Citalopram (Celexa), and Escitalopram (Lexapro).
